title: Nishimori Threshold Estimation for Bayesian Inference and $\mathbb{Z}_q$ Surface Code Decoding
abstract: In quantum error correction, the error threshold provides essential quantitative guidance for the ability to bring about fault-tolerance through decoding the effects of incoherent noise, weak measurement or inference. However, the numerical value of an error threshold is typically only accessible through large-scale numerical simulations of the underlying noise model. Here we introduce an analytical estimate of error thresholds falling into the Nishimori universality class via a Fourier--Walsh projection scheme that maps the critical point of the underlying disorder-free statistical-mechanics model to the Born-disordered Nishimori critical point. Using a minimal replica theory approach, this closed-form estimate is obtained from a projection of the exact replicated single-bond weight which we find to reproduce (within a percentage point) the known numerical thresholds of random-bond and random-plaquette Ising models / $\mathbb Z_2$ stabilizer codes in spatial dimensions $d=2-5$, and extends to Potts variables with $q\le4$. The main application of our projection scheme is to $\mathbb Z_q$ surface codes, whose decoding problem maps to the disordered $q$-state clock model. For $q\ge5$ the clean clock model has \textit{two} Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transitions, which the projection maps to two Nishimori temperatures that bound an intermediate information-critical phase. The resulting threshold values not only accurately agree with recent decohered-$\mathbb Z_q$-toric-code numerics, but are found to satisfy the Gilbert--Varshamov self-dual entropy relation $\ln q \simeq H_q(T_1^\ast)+H_q(T_2^\ast),$ although no duality condition is imposed in the construction. Our approach thereby points to a deeper connection between the clean and Born-disordered models, while allowing for instant analytical estimates of error thresholds for a variety of stabilizer codes.
summary: This work develops an analytical framework to estimate error thresholds in quantum error correction codes and Bayesian inference problems. It achieves this by projecting critical points from clean models onto their disordered Nishimori counterparts using Fourier-Walsh techniques. The resulting formulas provide accurate, closed-form estimates for a wide range of stabilizer codes, offering deep theoretical insight into noise resilience.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide analytical estimates for error thresholds in quantum error correction and Bayesian inference problems.
main_result: A Fourier-Walsh projection scheme is introduced that yields closed-form estimates for these thresholds, accurately reproducing known numerical results for various disordered models like Ising and $\mathbb{Z}_q$ codes.
method: The core method involves using a minimal replica theory approach combined with a Fourier-Walsh projection to map the critical point of a clean statistical mechanics model onto its Born-disordered Nishimori critical point.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to quantum error correction codes, specifically $\mathbb{Z}_q$ surface codes (mapped to the $q$-state clock model), as well as general disordered spin systems like Ising and Potts models on lattices.
key_observables: Error threshold ($\beta_{\text{Nishimori}}^c$), critical temperatures ($T^*_1, T^*_2$), and the satisfaction of the Gilbert-Varshamov self-dual entropy relation.
important_parameters: Measurement precision $\gamma$, Potts variable $q$ (especially $q \ge 5$), and spatial dimension $d$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on projecting the exact replicated single-bond weight using a minimal replica ansatz, which is highly successful but has limitations for first-order transitions ($q \le 4$).
figures_summary: Tables compare projection-based threshold estimates against numerical benchmarks for various disordered models (RBIM, RPGM, Potts, $\mathbb{Z}_q$ clock).
paper_structure: The paper develops the analytical framework by first analyzing the general mapping via Fourier-Walsh projection in the context of Bayesian inference. It then applies this scheme systematically to specific lattice models, detailing results for Ising, Potts ($q=3, 4$), and extending to $\mathbb{Z}_q$ clock models, culminating in discussions about multiple BKT transitions.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum error correction thresholds (a physical problem) and the analytical tools of disordered statistical mechanics (like Nishimori points) provides a powerful theoretical bridge for understanding fault tolerance limits.

Shown are the two transition temperatures T ∗ 1,2 of the two subsequent Nishimori transitions of the Zq clock model as a function of q. While the upper temperature saturates at T ∗ 1 →0.3832 (dotted), the lower projected Nishimori temperature is found to follow T ∗ 2 ≃A/q2 (dashed). The inset shows the GV self duality condition plotted as function of q which, ideally, should be 1. For more discussion see Appendix B.
